body:
# Independent audit: Hausdorff and mixed-integer normal-cone injection

Audited source: `candidate 5fcdb1b3fadb0891`.

**Result: PASS, all five sections.** No repair is needed. The result is a
finite-translation measure injection, not an OC center-selection result.

## 1. Sets, measures, and the finite support approximation

For compact nonempty A and B, A+B is compact and the projected cylinder
Z=pi^(-1)(pi(conv B)) is closed. Its intersection/difference with the fixed
closed halfspace is Borel. E_epsilon is Borel. Every decision region is a
finite intersection of strict and weak linear inequalities, including the
smallest-index tie rule, so every translated decision piece is Borel.
Thus every additivity statement uses measurable sets, including q=0.

A finite delta-net consisting of actual points of B gives a finite hull
P_F inside P with support error at most delta*||v||: approximate each term
of any convex combination by its chosen net point and apply the triangle
inequality. This argument does not need B convex or P full-dimensional.
Every vertex of the finite hull is an actual projected net point. Choosing
one fixed lift per distinct projected vertex is essential and is done.

## 2. The strict gap is against the original cylinder

For v=pi(a), the selected p satisfies v.p=h_(P_F)(v). Therefore

    v.pi(a+b_i)-h_P(v)
      >= ||v||^2-delta||v||
      >= ||v||(epsilon-delta)>0.

This excludes the ORIGINAL cylinder, including all its boundary. It holds
for every selected tie, for singleton P_F, and for lower-dimensional P_F.
It uses no null-hyperplane assertion. The assumption E+B subset H puts
every chosen image in the actual fixed halfspace.

## 3. Injectivity, ties, and exact measure preservation

The two maximizer inequalities imply

    (v-w).(p_i-p_j)>=0.

Coincident image points imply v-w=-(p_i-p_j), forcing p_i=p_j. The distinct
vertex list and one-lift convention then force the identical translation,
and the two original points coincide. This proof remains valid when all
support inequalities are equalities, so positive H_q mass on tie planes
is retained. On each of the finitely many disjoint source pieces the map
is exactly one Euclidean translation; their images are disjoint. Finite
additivity and translation invariance therefore give the full H_q source
mass, with no Jacobian loss and no claim that a general piecewise map is
an isometry across different pieces.

The sets E_(1/j) increase to E minus V. Continuity from below supplies the
claimed right side. This changes only input sets. No convergence of the
maps, target sets, bodies, halfspaces, or selected points is required.
The assumed finite H_q(A) makes every source quantity finite, although
this step itself would also be valid for an infinite measure.

## 4. Intrinsic and mixed-integer scope

For A,B subset Z^n x R^d, every actual chosen translation b_i belongs to
that additive group and hence preserves it. Hausdorff measure of any order
q is translation invariant. Nothing substitutes ambient Lebesgue measure
for H_q. The subtraction of E intersect V remains explicit: it must not
be discarded when it carries positive intrinsic measure. For q=0, finite
H_0(A) makes A finite, and the same proof is a literal injection of all
points outside V, including tie points.

A bounded subset of the mixed lattice has finitely many integer fibers.
Their embeddings are isometries, and distinct fibers are disjoint Borel
sets, so the q=d Hausdorff fiber-sum identity is valid (including d=0).
The midpoint qualification is correct: both summands in a common integer
parity class have an actual mixed-integer midpoint, and the H_q scaling
is exactly 2^(-q). The source makes no unjustified Gamma replacement.

## 5. Far-tail reserve

Translate the affine line containing S to V while translating A and the
halfspace by the same vector, and leave B fixed. This is the correct
translation of A+B and S+B. Since S+B lies inside V+conv B, the injected
set is disjoint from S+B and remains inside (A+B) intersect H. Since
S subset A, subtraction of their finite ambient cap volumes is exactly
the measure of their set difference. In dimension d>=2 the line has
zero d-dimensional measure, yielding the whole far-tail reserve.

For d=1, V is the full line and E minus V is empty; the theorem correctly
provides no false positive reserve. The same reasoning works for an
affine subspace of dimension less than q, and otherwise keeps the actual
subspace mass subtraction. No boundary-mass assumption enters this proof.

## 6. Added Borel-target and common-hull corollary

The updated statement allows any fixed Borel target H containing E+B.
The proof uses no halfspace property after that inclusion, so this is
valid with precisely the same finite map. In the added common residual
hull corollary, E+B and P+B are both inside the same open intersection G.
The affine span of P has dimension k-1<d, so it has zero source volume.
The injection supplies added volume at least |E| outside its original
cylinder, while all P+B remains inside that cylinder. The actual common
hull bound |P+B|>2^(k-1)b is used once. Scaling by 1/2 preserves the
homogeneous strict inequalities defining G and scales volume by 2^(-d),
giving the stated strict missed-volume bound.

A wording precision was sent to the author: the finite maps inject
E_epsilon; the proved conclusion gives volume at least |E| outside the
cylinder. It should not be described as constructing one limiting map
or a single translated copy of all E. No such limiting map is needed
for the inequality. The k=d+1 exclusion correctly retains the source
mass on the now full-dimensional affine span.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
